balance.introTitre: Are you made for living alone or with someone?
balance.introTexte: Twenty questions about your daily life, your habits and what you would or wouldn't put up with from someone else. The result comes as two shares that add up to a hundred: the one leaning towards living alone, the one leaning towards living together.
balance.q1: Have you ever lived with a partner, under the same roof?
balance.q1a: Yes, and I rather liked sharing the everyday.
balance.q1b: Yes, and that's when I understood I needed more space.
balance.q1c: No, never, but the idea appeals to me.
balance.q1d: No, and just thinking about it makes me uncomfortable.
balance.q2: Coming home to an empty place, how does that feel?
balance.q2a: It weighs on me: that's when I feel someone is missing.
balance.q2b: It depends on the day, some evenings the silence is heavy.
balance.q2c: It suits me, I find everything exactly where I left it.
balance.q2d: It's often the best moment of my day.
balance.q3: Your partner comes home and wants to tell you about their day, while you're in the middle of something else.
balance.q3a: I stop what I'm doing, that's exactly what I like about living together.
balance.q3b: I listen with one ear and finish what I started.
balance.q3c: I ask for ten minutes, and it usually goes fine.
balance.q3d: Being cut off like that every evening, no thanks.
balance.q4: How much time alone do you need to feel good?
balance.q4a: Not much: other people are what recharges me.
balance.q4b: An evening to myself now and then is enough.
balance.q4c: Several hours a day, otherwise I get irritable.
balance.q4d: Whole days, regularly, otherwise I'm saturated.
balance.q5: Would it bother you if your partner tidied up differently from you?
balance.q5a: No, we'd find our own way of doing things in a few weeks.
balance.q5b: At first yes, then I'd get used to it.
balance.q5c: Yes, and I'd probably bring it up often.
balance.q5d: Yes, it's the kind of detail that ends up wearing me down.
balance.q6: A decision that only concerns you: a job offer, a city to leave.
balance.q6a: I'd talk about it before deciding, the other person's opinion counts.
balance.q6b: I'd decide, then tell them straight away.
balance.q6c: I'd mention it once it's done.
balance.q6d: I don't want that kind of choice to be up for discussion.
balance.q7: What do your ideal evenings look like?
balance.q7a: Someone next to me, even with nothing special going on.
balance.q7b: Together most nights, with two or three evenings to myself a week.
balance.q7c: Mostly alone, with company when I feel like it.
balance.q7d: Alone, that's when I feel best.
balance.q8: How did your past relationships end?
balance.q8a: In disappointment, but I loved being with someone.
balance.q8b: A bit of both: good times, and real relief at the end.
balance.q8c: Mostly relief at getting my own life back.
balance.q8d: I haven't had a real relationship yet.
balance.q9: You get some good news. Your first reflex:
balance.q9a: Call someone: it doesn't exist until I've said it out loud.
balance.q9b: Keep it to myself for an hour, then share it.
balance.q9c: Mention it when the occasion comes up.
balance.q9d: Keep it, it's nobody else's business.
balance.q10: Letting someone know when you're coming home later than planned:
balance.q10a: Seems normal to me, I'd do it without thinking.
balance.q10b: I'd remember, even if it's not my first reflex.
balance.q10d: I don't want to account for my hours to anyone.
balance.q11: A whole Sunday with the same person, nothing planned:
balance.q11a: That's exactly what I'm looking for.
balance.q11b: I like it, as long as we don't have to talk the whole time.
balance.q11c: Half a day, then I need to go off on my own.
balance.q12a: I'd like someone to be there.
balance.q12b: A message or two is enough for me.
balance.q12d: I shut everything off and deal with it on my own.
balance.q13: Your partner has their own habits, they don't do things your way, and they won't change.
balance.q13a: That's fine by me, it's even what makes living together interesting.
balance.q13b: I adapt, as long as we agree on the essentials.
balance.q13c: I adapt badly: I'd struggle not to try to change them.
balance.q13d: I think I'd end up leaving.
balance.q14: Sharing a budget, the shopping, your sleeping hours:
balance.q14a: No problem at all, it comes with the territory.
balance.q14b: The shopping and the hours yes, but I'd keep my own budget.
balance.q14c: The shopping at a push, the rest no.
balance.q14d: I want all of that to stay mine.
balance.q15: When you see a couple who've been together fifteen years, you think:
balance.q15b: "Looks good, if it works for both of them."
balance.q15c: "To each their own way of living."
balance.q16: Where do you see yourself in ten years?
balance.q16a: In our home, with the same person.
balance.q16b: In a relationship, without knowing yet with whom or in what shape.
balance.q16c: In my own place, with someone who has theirs too.
balance.q16d: In my own place, alone, and perfectly happy with it.
balance.q17: What you miss most when you've been on your own for a long time:
balance.q17a: Someone to tell the small things of the day to.
balance.q17b: A presence, someone in the next room.
balance.q17c: Nothing specific, but some evenings feel hollow.
balance.q18: An argument, how does that leave you?
balance.q18a: It annoys me, we talk it out and things move on.
balance.q18b: It stays with me for a while, then it's fine.
balance.q18c: It takes me several days to come back from it.
balance.q18d: I'd rather never have to go through one at all.
balance.q19: In an ordinary week, what does your social life look like?
balance.q19a: I see people almost every day.
balance.q19b: Two or three times a week.
balance.q19c: Once, and that's enough for me.
balance.q19d: I can go a week without seeing anyone and not miss it.
balance.q20: What you're looking for right now, honestly:
balance.q20a: A life with someone, that's my priority.
balance.q20b: To meet someone, without making it urgent.
balance.q20c: I'm fine on my own, and I'm not closing the door.
balance.q20d: I'm fine on my own, and I'm not looking for anything.
balance.r1_d: Your answers lean clearly to one side: a life you organise for yourself. Your rhythm, your hours, your home, the way you recharge, all of it rests on a space you don't share, and it works. This isn't a failed test, and it doesn't say you're closed off to other people. Plenty of people who get this result have already lived with a partner and know exactly what it cost them. Living alone is a way of life, not a waiting room.
balance.r1_a: If someone does come along, don't assume everything would have to be put in common. Two homes, separate evenings written into the week, one holiday a year each on their own side: that exists, and it holds up very well. Bring it up early, rather than negotiating it later under pressure.
balance.r2_t: Mostly alone, with someone from time to time
balance.r2_d: You've got nothing against company, far from it. What gets in the way is the shared everyday: someone in the next room every evening, hours that line up with somebody else's, decisions that get discussed. Your answers say you enjoy time together and prefer to choose when it happens. This profile often does well in relationships that don't share everything: a steady story, but each in their own home, or a couple who see each other three evenings a week.
balance.r2_a: If you do move in with someone one day, look at the flat before anything else. A room whose door you can close changes more than any conversation about chores. And say it at the start, not six months in when the tension has already settled.
balance.r3_t: Together, with space for each of you
balance.r3_d: The two shares are almost level, and that isn't a soft result. It means you genuinely need both: someone to share your days with, and moments when nobody asks you for anything. This profile works very well as a couple, provided the need for solitude is said out loud and accepted rather than hidden. The trap is forcing yourself into six months of fusion, then cutting everything off at once because it has become unbreathable.
balance.r3_a: Set the frame early, without making a drama of it: one evening a week to yourself, a weekend now and then, a corner of the flat where nobody talks to you. Said at the start, it sounds obvious. Said after an argument, it sounds like a reproach.
balance.r4_t: Life with someone suits you, at your own pace
balance.r4_d: You're clearly more comfortable with company than on your own. Sharing your days, letting someone know, deciding together: none of that costs you anything, and it's often what puts you in a good mood. You still keep a few reflexes of your own, a need for silence here, a decision you'd rather take alone there, and that's a good sign. In couples who last, each person usually keeps a bit of room of their own, and nobody makes a problem of it.
balance.r4_a: One thing to keep in mind: when you enjoy life with someone, you tend to put their wishes first without noticing, and to realise it a year later. Keep what was yours before the relationship, an activity, friends, one evening in the week. That's what makes you good to live with, not the other way round.
balance.r5_t: You're made for living with someone
balance.r5_d: Everything leans the same way. Other people recharge you, you share your news the moment it arrives, the shared everyday doesn't scare you and you picture the future without hesitating. This isn't dependency: some people feel good when there's someone around, others when there's nobody, and you're in the first group. Worth knowing, it saves you from forcing yourself through spells alone "to learn something" that will teach you nothing.
balance.r5_a: The real risk with this profile is accepting a mediocre relationship because being alone weighs on you. If you know those spells cost you, put what you need in place before you need it: two or three friends you can call on a Sunday, an activity that gets you out of the house. That's what lets you choose the next person instead of putting up with them.
